result: In 19 CFS patients and 10 controls, IL-6 administration raised somatic symptoms in both groups (faster in CFS) but impaired cognition in neither, and CFS patients performed like controls on memory, attention and executive tests before, during and after the challenge.
reason: Experimental IL-6 challenge, not acute-infection prediction of post-infective fatigue; main measured result is no cognitive deficit vs controls, which bears on neuro-cognition (small sample).

result: In 22 monozygotic twin pairs discordant for CFS, antibodies to HHV-8, CMV, HSV-1/2 and HCV and PCR for HHV-6/7/8, CMV, EBV, HSV, VZV, JC, BK and parvovirus B19 did not differ between affected and healthy twins.
reason: Independent co-twin cohort, herpesvirus serology and viral DNA null, same direction; small and EBV tested only by PCR.

result: In 21 CFS patients vs 21 controls, baseline salivary cortisol profiles were normal but suppression after 0.5 mg dexamethasone was enhanced and prolonged.
reason: Same challenge measure (dexamethasone suppression), same direction, independent cohort.

result: With gold-standard cycle CPET, VO2max did not differ in 16 male CFS vs matched sedentary controls (40.5 vs 43.3 ml/kg/min) and was lower in 17 females (30.0 vs 34.2, p=0.002) but at 96-101% of age-predicted in both sexes; HRmax was lower only in males (184 vs 192); lactate threshold did not differ.
reason: Same measure; authors conclude VO2max, HRmax and LT are normal, though the female difference (~4 ml/kg/min) is partly consistent with the finding, so the contradiction is mixed.

result: VO2max, HRmax and lactate threshold in CFS were near age-predicted sedentary values (96-101%), with only females lower than matched sedentary controls (30.0 vs 34.2 ml/kg/min).
reason: Does not test whether deconditioning explains abnormalities (no capacity-matched, bed-rest or disease comparison design); its result is already captured by the low-peak-VO2 link.

result: At 5-year follow-up of a 60-person RCT (53 assessed), 68% after CBT vs 36% after relaxation rated themselves much or very much improved, with more complete recovery, fewer relapses and more weekly work hours after CBT, though few reached normal fatigue levels.
reason: Not a replication of PACE; it reports a CBT advantage persisting at 5 years on self-rated outcomes, which runs against the finding's claim that between-group differences vanish long term.

result: Gene expression of RNase L and PKR antiviral pathway enzymes was upregulated in 10 acute gastroenteritis patients but not in 22 CFS patients or 21 healthy controls.
reason: Tests the same antiviral pathway and finds no upregulation in CFS; measured gene expression rather than enzyme activity or fragments, and small.

result: First-degree relatives of 25 CFS cases had significantly higher rates of CDC-defined CFS than relatives of 36 medical controls, without greater familial loading for depression.
reason: Independent family-history study, same measure (familial aggregation), same direction; small and informant-based.

result: A systematic review of 44 controlled trials (2,801 participants, 38 outcomes on ~130 scales) found positive results for graded exercise and CBT with high validity scores, inconclusive evidence for immunoglobulin and hydrocortisone, and insufficient evidence for other interventions.
reason: Pre-PACE qualitative synthesis of the CBT/GET trial evidence the finding rests on; adds context rather than replicating PACE.

result: In 15 CFS patients vs 15 matched sedentary controls on a maximal treadmill CPET, peak cardiovascular and ventilatory values were significantly lower, chiefly a lower heart rate at equal relative and maximal workloads, with effort criteria met.
reason: Same measure (single maximal CPET), lower peak values and low peak HR, effort verified; independent small cohort.
